But do their policies line up with what you believe?
Vote Compass presents users with 30 propositions covering the defining issues of the campaign.
It is possible to agree with one party strongly on economic policy, another on healthcare and a third on the environment.
It is showing how your views compare with the policy positions the parties have taken.
University of Auckland political psychology lecturer Danny Osborne said the tool was designed to engage people with policy.

“It moves away from that horse-race sort of politics about who’s in the lead and who’s doing this and who’s doing that, and focuses specifically on the policies.” The tool is developed by Vox Pop Labs in consultation with a panel of New Zealand political scientists.
Researchers have assessed published policies and public statements, and reviewed them with the parties, in order to accurately position them on the issues that matter to New Zealanders.
When users were asked to name the single most important issue to them in that election, the cost of living ranked first.
Once you’ve completed the questionnaire, you can explore how your views compare with the political parties and where you sit in the political landscape.
You can also look more closely at individual issues, see where you agree or disagree with parties, and read the statements used to explain their positions.
In a new feature, you can also compare how your views line up with similar groups in society.
